body.x: Korea Lighting Inc. (CEO Dongwoo Lee), a company specializing in functional light semiconductor platforms, participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, and unveiled its light therapy–based brain health management solution, ‘Neurélux.’

Korea Lighting is a lighting technology company known for its expertise in developing functional light semiconductor platforms and solutions. Based on its proprietary ‘HS FRAME’ technology, which integrates LED chips, circuits, and heat dissipation structures into a single system, the company has introduced a range of high-value-added lighting products to the market. Through precise control of light wavelengths and energy, Korea Lighting has demonstrated competitiveness across diverse application areas, including beauty, wellness, and healthcare.

In particular, HS FRAME technology enables compact product form factors while delivering high-output wavelengths, making it highly applicable to medical and healthcare fields. Building on this foundation, Korea Lighting continues to advance its core technologies and expand the application scope of functional lighting as it targets global markets.

At CES 2026, Korea Lighting showcased Neurélux, a product positioned under the concept of ‘Ambient Brain Healthcare.’ Neurélux is a light therapy solution designed to enable non-invasive brain health management within everyday living spaces. These capabilities stem from Neurélux’s dual infrared structure.

Neurélux emits two infrared wavelengths, 810 nanometers and 1,064 nanometers. The 810-nanometer wavelength activates mitochondria within brain cells, supporting neuroprotection and regeneration. At the same time, it promotes ATP production, the cellular energy unit, which helps reduce inflammation and support tissue recovery.

body.cap: The Korea Lighting booth at CES 2026 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The 1,064-nanometer wavelength penetrates more deeply into brain tissue, enabling subtle thermal stimulation and the activation of ion channels. This increases blood flow and enhances neuroplasticity, improving cognitive functions such as concentration and working memory. Additional strengths of Neurélux include its ability to maintain consistent wavelengths during prolonged use and its versatility, as it can also function as a standard lighting stand.

Leveraging these combined functionalities and use cases, Korea Lighting plans to use CES 2026 as a springboard to expand into broader areas of brain health care, including sleep disorder management and cognitive function care.

Dongwoo Lee, CEO of Korea Lighting, said, “Neurélux is a solution designed to help manage Alzheimer’s disease and sleep disorders, which have emerged as major challenges in an aging society, within the context of daily life.” He added, “Our goal is to transform the paradigm of the related market with the industry’s first non-contact brain healthcare product.”

He continued, “CES 2026 serves as both the first global stage for Neurélux and an opportunity to discuss strategic partnerships with healthcare companies and buyers in North America and Europe,” adding, “Korea Lighting will focus on demonstrating the maturity and value of its product throughout the event.”
